What an automated WCAG scan found on your homepage

Site  thesterlingfirm.com Scanned  July 13, 2026 Engine  axe-core (WCAG 2.1 A/AA) Prepared by  Norsoft

The homepage returned nine distinct accessibility issues across sixteen elements. The one worth looking at first is your intake form. It's the exact page where a prospective client turns into a case. Details below, grouped by severity.

Serious

Intake form fields have no labels

WCAG 1.3.1WCAG 4.1.24 fields

All four fields on your contact form rely on placeholder text, with no label a screen reader can read. Placeholder text also vanishes the moment someone starts typing. A blind or low-vision visitor can't tell which box is the name, the phone, or the case details, on the highest-value page you have. This is also the pattern accessibility testers look for first.

Text below the minimum contrast ratio

WCAG 1.4.32 elements

Two text elements fall under the 4.5:1 contrast minimum. Hard to read for anyone with low vision, or for a visitor on a phone in daylight.

Embedded frame has no accessible name

WCAG 4.1.21 element

An embedded frame (typically a map or video) carries no title, so a screen reader announces only “frame” with no idea what it holds.

A link is identified by color alone

WCAG 1.4.11 element

One link is set apart from the surrounding text only by its color. Colorblind visitors, or anyone in high-contrast mode, can't tell it's a link.

Moderate

Heading levels are out of order

WCAG 1.3.11 element

The page's headings skip levels. Screen-reader users navigate by heading structure, and a broken outline makes the page harder to move through.

Duplicate and misplaced page landmarks

WCAG 1.3.14 elements

The page has more than one footer region and other repeated landmarks. Assistive tech uses landmarks as navigation shortcuts, and duplicates create confusion about where a visitor is.

Minor

Invalid ARIA roles

WCAG 4.1.26 elements

Six elements use ARIA roles that aren't valid for those element types. Assistive technology may ignore or misread them.

Scope & method

This is an automated scan of a single page (the homepage), run with axe-core, the open-source engine from Deque Systems that most accessibility teams treat as the industry standard, checked against WCAG 2.1 Levels A and AA. It reflects the page as rendered on the scan date.

A full picture needs every page template scanned plus manual testing with real assistive technology (screen readers, keyboard-only navigation). And these are technical exposure signals, not a legal determination. Whether and how the ADA applies to your firm is a call for your judgment and your counsel. We're flagging what the tools see so nothing sits unnoticed.

Where we'd start

Norsoft builds and fixes software for a living. Two ways we can help: run a full audit across every page and hand you a prioritized fix list, or rebuild the site accessible by default and fully yours to own. Either way, the intake form is the first thing to fix.
